structure.title: A life addressed to God
structure.text: Books 1–9 revisit childhood, ambition, attachments, and conversion through a present act of prayer and interpretation.

structure.title: Memory, time, and creation
structure.text: Books 10–13 change from sustained life narrative into examinations of memory, time, and Genesis. The inquiry continues in another form.

people.name: Augustine
people.text: A bishop in North Africa looking back on his restless youth, his ambitions and his long resistance to faith, and addressing it all to God.

people.name: Monica
people.text: Augustine's devout mother, who prays and weeps for her son for years and follows him from Africa to Italy.

people.name: Grace
people.text: God's unearned help, which Augustine comes to believe he could neither deserve nor reach on his own, however clever he was.

context.title: Confession and praise
context.text: Confession includes acknowledging fault, declaring belief, and praising God. The address shapes what Augustine remembers and asks.
context.takeaway: The reader overhears an address to God.

context.title: Changing explanations
context.text: Augustine revisits earlier intellectual commitments from a later Christian position. His present interpretation and former experience are not identical.
context.takeaway: Keep both versions of the self visible.

notice.why: Intellectual difficulty and attachment can support each other.

notice.text: Follow the transition out of autobiography.
notice.why: The book's final inquiries ask what makes remembering and interpreting a life possible.

opening: Augustine wants a different life, but he would prefer to keep the pleasures of this one a little longer. He has explanations for the delay, intellectual questions to resolve, and ambitions that make conversion inconvenient. Writing to God, he revisits the child who stole, the young man who wanted admiration, and the adult who could recognise an evasion while continuing to rely on it. The intimacy comes from a mind refusing to let its eventual transformation tidy away the embarrassment of how long it resisted.
